svg.text: A disabled benchmark against a server you start and tune by hand

g.text: This one drives a server you started yourself, so it is disabled until somebody removes the annotation.
new ServerWrapper("localhost", 2481, 50051) - no Testcontainers, no container lifecycle in the test at all
The point is the JVM and engine settings the javadoc prescribes, which a container run would not reproduce.
Five times the photo volume of the containerised run: 5000 users and 250000 photos.
numOfThreads = 5, numOfUsers = 1000, numOfPhotos = 50 on a pool of 10; HTTP only, no protocol matrix
A fixed 30 second sleep gives the writers a head start, so the edge tasks find ids to attach to.
TimeUnit.SECONDS.sleep(30) before submitting createFriendships(2000) and createLike(2000)
The meter dump comes before the assertions here, so a failed run still leaves the timing numbers behind.
Metrics dump, then assertThatUserCountIs(5000) / PhotoCountIs(250000) / FriendshipCountIs(2000) / LikesCountIs(2000)
